title: No More Chinese Tailwinds
summary:
Tanker market may have to live without Chinese growth
For several decades China's rapid economic expansion and corresponding oil demand growth was the key driver of global ton-mile demand. China's rapid industrialization and urbanization, which started in the late 1990s and accelerated after China's entry into the World Trade Organization (WTO) in 2001, generated huge demand for global commodities, including oil. This so-called "Commodity Supercycle", which lasted until about 2014, peaked in 2008-2011.
